sources.entry: Wakupator - Wake On LAN Machine Manager based on network traffic. MIT C

summary.one_liner: Wakupator is a Linux service that wakes sleeping LAN machines via Wake-on-LAN when traffic to their IP/port is detected, by spoofing their IP addresses while they are powered off.
summary.what_it_does: Machines on the same LAN register themselves over TCP with a JSON payload (MAC address, name, and a list of IPs with ports) shortly before shutting down. After the machine goes offline, Wakupator spoofs the registered IPv4/IPv6 addresses and monitors traffic to the listed ports. When matching traffic arrives, it sends Wake-on-LAN magic packets, retrying a configurable number of times at a set interval. It logs the wake-up time and total monitoring duration, and also detects when a machine is started manually. Its main goal, per the README, is reducing energy use at the cost of availability.
use_cases: wake a home server on demand when a service is accessed
save electricity on machines that are not needed 24/7
wake a machine via SSH connection attempt
auto-start a Minecraft server when a player connects
how_to_run: Optionally run as a systemd service with AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_RAW CAP_NET_ADMIN (example unit in README)
Pre-compiled binaries are available from the project's release tab
notable: Spoofs IP addresses of powered-off machines so traffic reaches Wakupator before the host firewall
Works with IPv4 and IPv6, monitoring both TCP and UDP traffic
Registration is done by sending a JSON payload over TCP; example systemd service and Python script are provided in example/machine
Configurable wake attempts, retry interval, shutdown timeout, and probe delay
Detects when a machine is powered on manually, not only via Wakupator
caveats: Linux only, and the monitored machine needs Wake-on-LAN enabled in BIOS/UEFI and the OS
Sensitive to unsolicited internet scans, which can cause unwanted wake-ups; it must stay on the LAN and should not be exposed to the internet
For IPv6 monitoring with manual boots, Duplicate Address Detection must be disabled on the client; the router must not have static IP/MAC bindings on spoofed addresses
keywords: wake up pc on network request
